accepted.question_text: Determine the exact number of closed knight's tours on the standard 8×8 chessboard, where a closed knight's tour is a cyclic sequence of legal knight moves that visits every square exactly once and returns to the starting square.

evidence.quote: 513. See also Problems 48 and 369 (and associated comments), which deal with closed knight’s tours. Backtracking for n×n closed knight’s tours is only practical for n = 6 (there are no tours for smaller n), in which case there are 9,862 closed knight’s tours. It is not known exactly how many 8×8 tours exist.

accepted.question_text: Is P equal to NP, where P is the class of yes/no decision problems solvable in polynomial time and NP is the class of yes/no decision problems whose polynomial-length witnesses can be verified in polynomial time?

evidence.quote: Clearly, P ⊆ NP. It is not known whether P = NP, although the consensus of opinion is that probably P ≠ NP.

accepted.question_text: Determine the minimum possible number of moves required, in the worst case over all legal starting configurations, to solve the 15-puzzle, the sliding-tile puzzle on a 4×4 board with tiles 1 through 15 and one empty square.

evidence.quote: The minimum number of moves needed to solve the 15-puzzle in the worst case is unknown, but has been the subject of various papers in the AI literature.
